recreation_brief:
1. Set the full-slide background to light gray #E8E8E8.
2. Place the title 'Vector Notation for Linear Regression and Classification (One Sample)' at the top, spanning the full slide width, bold sans-serif: render 'Vector Notation for Linear Regression and Classification' in dark red #8B0000 and '(One Sample)' in dark blue #0000FF.
3. Place a yellow circle (#FFFF00 fill; exact yellow not captured) at the top-right corner of the slide, with the number '15' centered inside in black #000000.
4. Draw Box 1: a pale yellow #FFFFCC rectangle with a thin black #000000 border in the upper band of the left column (~10-40% of slide width).
5. In Box 1, place the header 'Model' in red italic #FF0000.
6. In Box 1, below the header, place the single line 'I/P: ( x1 x2 x3 ..... xn )   O/P: ( y )': render 'I/P:' and 'O/P:' in blue #0000FF and the vectors '( x1 x2 x3 ..... xn )' and '( y )' in red #FF0000 (token split assumed; see validation).
7. Draw Box 2: a pale yellow #FFFFCC rectangle with a thin black #000000 border in the middle band of the left column (~10-40% of slide width), stacked directly below Box 1.
8. In Box 2, place the header 'Model' in red italic #FF0000.
9. In Box 2, below the header, place 'y = w1x1 + w2x2 + w2x2 + ... + wdxd + b' exactly as written (the duplicated 'w2x2' term is kept verbatim as extracted), with w-terms in blue #0000FF, x-terms in red #FF0000, and 'b' in green #008000.
10. In Box 2, below that equation, place 'y = W^T X + b' with 'W^T' in blue #0000FF, 'X' in red #FF0000, and 'b' in green #008000.
11. Draw Box 3: a pale yellow #FFFFCC rectangle with a thin black #000000 border in the lower band of the left column (~10-40% of slide width), stacked directly below Box 2.
12. In Box 3, place 'y = ( w1 w2 .... wd ) · ( x1 x2 ... xd )^T + b' with w-terms in blue #0000FF, x-terms in red #FF0000, and 'b' in green #008000.
13. Draw Box 4: a large pale yellow #FFFFCC rectangle with a thin black #000000 border on the right side of the slide (~45-85% of slide width), larger than any single left box.
14. In Box 4, place 'Input:' in red #FF0000, followed by 'X =' and a vertical column vector reading x1, x2, x3, ..., xd from top to bottom, all in red #FF0000 (i.e., X = ( x1 x2 x3 ... xd )^T, a column vector).
15. In Box 4, below the X vector, place 'W =' followed by a vertical column vector reading W1, W2, W3, ..., Wd from top to bottom, all in blue #0000FF (i.e., W = ( W1 W2 W3 ... Wd )^T, a column vector).
16. In Box 4, below the W vector, place 'Output:' followed by '( y )', both in red #FF0000.

fixes_applied: Filled subtitle_or_header (was null): documented that no subtitle exists and that 'Model' serves only as the in-box header of the upper-left and middle-left boxes, per layout.regions and visual_elements.

Rewrote recreation_brief from 10 multi-element steps into a 16-step ordered checklist; each step places exactly one element with its exact text, position band, hex colors, and shape.
Specified concrete defaults for details the source omitted: circle fill #FFFF00, circle digits black #000000, box borders thin black #000000 — each flagged in uncertain_items.
Assigned token colors inside the I/P-O/P box (labels blue, vectors red) from the captured box palette #FF0000/#0000FF; flagged as an assumption.
Preserved the duplicated term 'w2x2 + w2x2' verbatim in bullets, equations, and the brief (not 'corrected' to w3x3) to avoid inventing content; flagged in uncertain_items.
uncertain_items: The linear equation contains the duplicated term 'w2x2 + w2x2' in both verbatim_text.bullets[3] and equations[1]; it is likely a source-slide typo for 'w3x3' or an extraction artifact, but this cannot be verified without the image, so it was kept verbatim.
Exact yellow of the '15' circle and the digit color are not captured (source says only 'yellow circle'); #FFFF00 fill and black #000000 digits are used as defaults.
Token-level red/blue split inside the I/P-O/P box is not captured; only the box palette (#FF0000, #0000FF) is known. The brief assumes 'I/P:'/'O/P:' in blue and the vectors in red.
Box borders are described only as 'thin dark borders'; rendered as thin black #000000.

The I/P line uses subscript n (x1 ... xn) while all model equations use subscript d (x1 ... xd); this mix is consistent across bullets and equations and was kept verbatim, but the source slide cannot be re-checked.
